gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI AC180 takes solar only through a 12–60 V DC, 10 A, 500 W window, so its two-panel kit needs the two SP200L panels (24.6 V Voc each) wired in series. That gives 49.2 V Voc, inside the window. Wired in parallel, the 10 A cap limits charging to roughly 246 W at most. A third panel in series reaches 73.8 V Voc, which breaks the manual's 60 V limit.
standout_why: I read both cited rival pages. solar.com's 2026 guide covers microinverters, UL 3700 and state rules. It names no panel voltage, connector, input window or series/parallel wiring, and it does not treat battery kits as plug-in options. pluginsolartracker.com's California page covers only UL certification and the 1,200 W AC output cap, with nothing on DC compatibility. ChatGPT's own answer shows battery kits (EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic + 160 W, Anker C300 + 60 W) but gives no pairing rule. The series-wiring rule decides the panel count (1, 2 or 3 × 200 W) and how the kit is wired.
kit_items: power station: BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W). Its solar input is 12–60 V DC, 10 A, 500 W max on a DC7909 port, and the box includes a 1.5 m solar charging cable. Two 200 W panels (400 W) fit under the 500 W cap.

solar panels: 2× BLUETTI SP200L 200 W foldable (MC4, 24.6 V Voc, 10.8 A Isc). BLUETTI lists the AC180 as a compatible model. Wired in series they give 49.2 V Voc, under the AC180's 60 V limit, at about 10 A. Do not wire them in parallel (10.8 + 10.8 = 21.6 A Isc against a 10 A cap) and do not add a third panel in series (73.8 V Voc).
balcony fit check: each SP200L is 2,105 mm (82.8 in) long unfolded and 8.14 kg, so the balcony needs about 2.1 m of clear length per panel.

findings.label: series vs parallel arithmetic
findings.value: Series: 2 × 24.6 = 49.2 V Voc (under 60 V), current ≤ 10.8 A Isc (about the 10 A cap). Parallel: 2 × 10.8 = 21.6 A Isc against a 10 A cap, so charging is capped at about 10 A × 24.6 V = 246 W at most. Three in series: 3 × 24.6 = 73.8 V Voc (over 60 V, not allowed).
findings.source_title: BLUETTI 200W Portable Solar Panel (Voc/Isc) + AC180 manual limits above
findings.note: My arithmetic from the two maker figures. 246 W is a ceiling that uses Voc; real parallel output is lower because the operating voltage is below Voc.
